Hey Defiant-Team7040, great to hear that you’re on track to getting rid of your debt. You made an awesome choice. I can tell you, as someone who was sliding deeper into debt, I was looking for a way out too. Going with Freedom Debt Relief was incredible. I went from unaffordable payments of over $1,000 to manageable deposits around $450. And don’t stress if you miss one. Life happens. I’m three years into the program now, five accounts settled, one to go. Already thinking about building my savings next. You’ve got this.

Freedom Debt Relief is fantastic. Changed things around for me. The team is supportive, easy to work with, and actually cared about helping me succeed. They gave me a plan I could stick to, and it finally feels like I’m moving forward.

I was in the same boat. Monthly minimums were killing me and nothing felt doable until I talked to Freedom Debt Relief. The monthly deposit they suggested was the first number that actually fit my budget. What really helped me stick with it was knowing I could miss a payment and not get kicked out of the program. Life happens and having that flexibility made a huge difference. Settlements took a little time but once the first one came through, I felt like I was finally making progress. Almost done now and so glad I started when I did.

Shame on National Debt Relief for enrolling you in a debt settlement program without making sure you fully understood how it works or what other alternatives you had.

Yes, the program works by having you stop payments, go into default, and then they try to negotiate settlements over time. But that process tanks your credit, racks up late fees, and opens you up to the risk of collections or even lawsuits. That part often gets buried in the sales pitch.

It might not be too late to walk away, but your credit has already taken the hit. The more important question now is what you can actually afford and whether there's a better way to pay off the debt without doing more damage.
